chapter_theme: Kurinji in the secret love: the girl's pallor, slipping bangles and wasting shoulders tell of the hill lord (1, 5, 7), her heart goes to him or pines bound by longing (3, 6), she wonders whether he will come or has turned from her (2, 9) and is sure he will come at midnight (10), while the friend comforts her (4), names him as the only cure (8), notes the house that keeps her (11) and warns of an angry kinsman's spear (12).

1.reading: The friend says that on the slope by the millet field where parrots eager to feed are driven off and the matchless young doe moves, the girl's body wastes and turns pale, as if announcing that the lord of the forest land is the one who joined with her.
1.nuance: The pallor does the talking: the secret union is written on her body in a way the field-watch was meant to prevent, so the line works as a push toward marriage. இவன், 'this man', may point at the hero standing there, which is why the friend is taken as the speaker; the girl herself could equally be saying it.

thinai_evidence.note: the guarded millet field and the hill slope are kurinji ground

iraicchi.act: the waterfall bears sandalwood down to the burnt clearing and makes it fragrant
iraicchi.sense: the hill's own stream heals the scorched field as the hero ought to come and soothe the girl he has left burning, so his absence is the deceit

2.reading: The girl asks her friend whether the deceitful hill lord, from whose hill the waterfall carries sandalwood down so that the burnt clearing grows fragrant, will not come, for her heart comes trembling.
2.nuance: வஞ்ச, deceitful, sits right against the stream's kindness: the water brings sweetness to scorched ground unasked, while he, who scorched her, does not come.

thinai_evidence.note: sandal, the hill stream and the burnt millet clearing are kurinji things

ullurai.tenor: the girl herself, who tasted union and is now bound by longing

pairs.situation: she has tasted the sweetness of union with him
she is now caught in the bond of desire and cannot free herself

ullurai.speaker_fit: the girl uses a monkey of her own hill, a thing she knows (porul 7.26)

3.reading: The girl says that her heart pines with longing for the lord of the hill of trap-stones, where by the green moss-grown spring the fierce female monkey, used to the place, tastes the fruit and, caught in the noose, runs.
3.nuance: பாசம் is both the hunter's noose and attachment, so the snared monkey and the 'bond' of love are one word. The subject of the running in line 3 is not certain; if it is not the monkey, the hidden comparison weakens to a mood.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill monkey, the mountain spring and the hill lord fix kurinji

4.reading: The friend asks the jewelled girl whether the hill lord, from whose hill the langur leaps off the sweet-fruited mango to take the pleasure of the tall jackfruit, is a man to join with her and then forget, he who assured her with words mixed with honey.
4.nuance: The friend's comfort carries a shadow: the langur that leaves one sweet tree for a sweeter one is the very fickleness she says he lacks. It is a single mood with no second pair and no stated situation, so it is not tagged as ullurai.

thinai_evidence.note: jackfruit and the langur of the hill trees are kurinji things

5.reading: The girl says that for the lord of the hill where the waterfall roars like a drum and the dark she-elephant comes tending a honeycomb loud with bees and full of sweet honey, her shoulders lie as though in hell.
5.nuance: Hell is a startling vehicle in a love quatrain and belongs to the later moral vocabulary of the didactic books. குரல் in line 1 may be the bees' hum or a millet ear, and the first two lines do not settle what the elephant carries.

thinai_evidence.note: the she-elephant, honey and the hill falls are kurinji things

6.reading: The girl says that, unspoken, her heart goes to the jewelled broad chest of the faultless hill lord, from whose grove thick with trees the wild cow leaps and the famed young female monkey runs and leaps.
6.nuance: உகளும் is repeated for the wild cow and the monkey, and the heart's going is the third leap; the creatures carry a mood of unchecked movement only, so they are scene. உரையா, without telling, makes the heart a secret traveller, which is the whole of kalavu.

thinai_evidence.note: the wild cow, the monkey and the hill grove are kurinji things

iraicchi.act: the male monkey takes the sweet fruit in its cheek and runs away at once
iraicchi.sense: the hero, like the monkey, took his pleasure and made off, which is why the mere mention of his friendship loosens her bangles

7.reading: The girl says that when the friendship of the hill lord is spoken of, her bangles slip off: in his land the male monkey climbs the rock, stuffs the sweet ripe banana into its cheek in the daylight and runs off with a rush.
7.nuance: கேண்மை, friendship, is ironic after the picture of the monkey that grabs and bolts.

thinai_evidence.note: the male monkey, the plantain and the rock cliff are kurinji things

8.reading: The friend says that if the lord of the great rocky hill, where the black-trunked angry elephant and the dark snake are named in a line now partly lost, comes caring for the girl, the sickness she suffers will shrink.
8.nuance: The cure named is the man, not a rite: பேணி வரினே, if he comes cherishing her, reads as coming to wed. The addressee may be the hero, urged to marry, or the foster mother, told the true cause of the illness; the poem does not decide.

thinai_evidence.note: the angry elephant and the great rock hill are kurinji

pairs.situation: he takes a harmless thing for a danger
he has fled from their union and stays away

ullurai.speaker_fit: the girl uses an elephant of her own hill, a thing she knows (porul 7.26)

9.reading: The girl asks her friend whether the lord of the good fruitful hill, where the angry elephant, taking the kaanthal's bud for smoke, lays its trunk between its raised tusks, looks to its herd and leaps up and flees, has grown averse to union with them.
9.nuance: The word division of line 1 is unsure (அரும்பு புகை, the bud as smoke, or அரும்பு உகை, the bud rising); the elephant's flight from a harmless flower is what the hidden comparison rests on.

thinai_evidence.note: the kaanthal and the hill elephant are kurinji things

comparisons.tenor: the red kaanthal bud, mistaken for fire

10.reading: The girl tells her friend that the lord of the hill whose millet fields are ringed by vengai with golden clusters will come right now at midnight, bearing a spear like lightning, so how could her eyelids close.
10.nuance: இமைபொரு, eyelids meeting, may mean she lies sleepless waiting or that only his coming lets her sleep; either way the midnight tryst is fixed in her mind before it happens.

thinai_evidence.note: the hill and the midnight tryst are kurinji's land and hour

11.reading: The friend asks whether the lord of the good hill bright with tender leaves, where the spotted peacock delights in scratching the ground a fierce boar has dug up, will come, since coming is hard for him to this house of theirs.
11.nuance: The peacock that takes its pleasure in ground the boar has turned is a picture of one creature enjoying another's labour; it has no single act a person of the situation does, so it stays scene. The house in line 4 suggests the girl is now kept indoors.

thinai_evidence.note: the boar, the peacock and the young leaves are kurinji things

12.reading: The friend warns that a man, angry, comes with a sharp spear in hand, asking whether the chest of that bright handsome one who wears fragrant naagam flowers mixed with fresh vengai blossoms in his hair can be ended.
12.nuance: Who the angry spearman is the poem does not say; he is most simply one of the girl's kin who has learned of the visits, and the warning is the friend's way of shutting the night path.

thinai_evidence.note: the vengai and naagam flowers worn in the hair are the kurinji hero's

links.note: Kural 1182 has pallor ride the woman's body proud that 'he gave it'; Kainnilai 1 has her body waste pale as if saying 'the forest lord joined with her'.
links.teaches: Set in the guarded millet field of the secret love, the Kural's private conceit of pallor naming its giver becomes a public danger, since a body that names the lover undoes the secrecy that kalavu depends on.

links.note: Both set a hill creature that has handled ripe fruit against snares; in Kuruntokai the hunter sets nets on every tree after the fruit is already touched, in Kainnilai the monkey tastes the fruit and is caught.
links.teaches: The same fruit-and-snare economy of the hill serves two speakers opposite ways: the friend uses the late snares to tell the man the girl is now guarded too late, while the girl uses the caught monkey to say she herself is the one bound by the sweetness she tasted.

links.note: Kuruntokai 42's friend asks the hero whether their bond will wane even if desire ends; Kainnilai 4's friend asks the girl whether he is one to join and then forget.
links.teaches: The one doubt about the man's constancy is put by the friend as a challenge to him in Kuruntokai and as a comfort to the girl in Kainnilai, so the pair shows the friend's double office of pressing the hero and calming the heroine with the same question.

links.note: Kural 1249's woman asks her heart whom it goes seeking when he is within it; Kainnilai 6's girl lets her heart go unspoken to his jewelled chest.
links.teaches: The heart's going out to the lover is chided as foolish in the Kural's separation chapter but is a silent secret gift in Kainnilai's secret stage, so the same movement of the heart is judged by whether he is still near.

links.note: In Kural 1157 the slipping bangles proclaim that the lord of the shore has left; in Kainnilai 7 they slip at the mere telling of the hill lord's friendship.
links.teaches: The Kural gives the bangles as a sign without a scene, and Kainnilai supplies the scene that explains them: a monkey that snatches the fruit and bolts, so the bangles fall because the 'friendship' was a theft and the leaving was already in it.

links.note: Both have the hill lord of the vengai coming at midnight with spear in hand; Kainnilai 10 is the girl's eager forecast, Akananuru 298 her words when he has come, sweet yet unable to speak her love for fear of the mother.
links.teaches: Read together the two give the before and after of the night tryst: the quatrain's sleepless certainty that he will come turns, once he is there, into fear of the household and a plea for marriage, so the midnight visit is never the end the girl longs for.

source_issues: 1-12: the core records carry no colophon thurai, so thurai_akam speaker, addressee and stage are inferred from the poems and occasion.words is null throughout.
1 line 2: எரியும் ('burns') makes poor sense of the doe on the slope; a form such as வெரூஉம் ('fears') or a verb of roaming may lie behind it.
3 line 1: அழிமுதுநீர் is obscure; line 3 பாசம்பட் டோ டும் has a stray space splitting டோ, read பாசம்பட்டோடும்.
8 line 2: largely lost (கி...க்...கொண்...கரும்); the description of the elephant and snake cannot be recovered and no comparison is read from it.
9 line 1: காந்தள ரும்புகை may divide as காந்தள் அரும்பு புகை (the bud as smoke) or அரும்பு உகை; the reading taken is the first.
11 line 4: அரிதுரைத்திவ் is hard to divide (அரிது உரைத்து இவ்); the sense that his coming to this house is hard is a guess.
